name: SOLAR PANEL TEST CHAMBER
desc: Smart Programmable Solar Panel Environmental Climatic Test Chamber engineered for lifespan validation of photovoltaic modules in compliance with IEC 61215:2005 protocols. Features a high-capacity SS304 workspace handling up to 8 solar panels, powered by a French TECUMSEH compressor.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS SOLAR PANEL TEST CHAMBER is a precision-engineered environmental simulation system designed to validate the long-term reliability and performance of photovoltaic modules under accelerated stress conditions. Operating on the principle of controlled climatic cycling, it subjects solar panels to extreme temperature fluctuations (from -60°C to +100°C), high humidity levels (20% to 98% RH), and combined thermal-humidity profiles as mandated by international standards such as IEC 61215:2005, IEC 61730, and ASTM E1171. The chamber employs a cascade mechanical compression refrigeration system using eco-safe refrigerants R404A and R23, driven by a French TECUMSEH compressor, to achieve rapid thermal transitions at rates of 1.0 to 3.4°C per minute. High-precision Class A PT100 RTD sensors and dry/wet bulb humidity sensors provide real-time feedback to an intelligent PID controller, ensuring temperature stability within ±0.5°C and humidity deviation within ±2.5% RH. Forced air convection via a centrifugal blower ensures uniform spatial distribution across the SS304 workspace, which accommodates up to eight 1×2 meter panels. This chamber is indispensable for solar panel manufacturers, quality assurance engineers, and research scientists (including B.Sc/M.Sc students and PhD researchers) who need to assess module degradation mechanisms such as solder joint fatigue, delamination, corrosion of busbars, and moisture ingress. It specifically replicates three critical IEC 61215 test protocols: Thermal Cycle Test (50 or 200 cycles from -40°C to +85°C), Humidity Freeze Test (10 cycles from +85°C/85% RH to -40°C), and Damp Heat Test (1000 hours at 85°C/85% RH). By exposing panels to these harsh conditions, the chamber accelerates aging processes that would normally take decades in the field, allowing researchers to predict service life, identify failure modes, and optimize materials like encapsulants (EVA, POE), backsheets, and junction boxes.
sop: Ensure the chamber is connected to a stable power supply and the water reservoir for humidity generation is filled with deionized or distilled water to prevent mineral buildup.
Open the chamber door and carefully load the solar panels onto the designated racks, ensuring they are securely positioned and spaced to allow uniform airflow; close and lock the door.
Power on the main switch and wait for the controller to initialize; the color LCD touch screen will display the home screen.
Press the 'SET' button once on the PID controller to enter the setpoint mode for temperature.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrow keys to adjust the target temperature to the desired value (e.g., 85°C for damp heat test or -40°C for thermal cycling).
Press 'SET' again to lock the temperature setpoint and proceed to the humidity setpoint (if applicable).
If humidity control is required, press the 'SET' button again to access the humidity setpoint mode, then use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to set the target relative humidity (e.g., 85% RH).
Press 'SET' once more to confirm and lock the humidity value; the controller will now display the current and setpoint values.

To run a predefined test program (e.g., IEC 61215 Thermal Cycle), navigate to the program menu on the touch screen, select the desired program number (e.g., Program 1 for 200 cycles), and press 'RUN' to start.
Monitor the chamber's real-time temperature and humidity readings on the display; ensure the compressor and blower are operating normally without unusual vibrations or noises.
During the test, do not open the chamber door unless absolutely necessary, as this will disrupt the controlled environment and may cause thermal shock to the panels.

After the test cycle is complete, allow the chamber to return to ambient temperature and humidity before opening the door; use the controller to stop the program and switch off the heaters and compressor.
Carefully unload the solar panels using appropriate handling equipment (gloves, suction lifters) to avoid damage or contamination.
Clean the interior SS304 surfaces with a soft cloth and mild detergent if any residue is present; ensure the water reservoir is drained and refilled for the next use.
Log the test data via USB or Ethernet connection for analysis and record any anomalies in the chamber's performance.

SAFETY WARNING: Never operate the chamber with the door interlock bypassed or with panels that have exposed live electrical connections; always disconnect the panels from any external load and ensure proper grounding before testing to prevent electric shock or fire hazards. Additionally, avoid direct contact with the chamber's internal surfaces during or immediately after high-temperature or sub-zero cycles, as they can cause severe burns or frostbite.
